title: Discovering Opinion Intervals from Conflicts in Signed Graphs

predicted_errors.error_location: Section 2.1 (Theorem 2.2 and surrounding text) and the statement that the proof is in Appendix A
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The paper presents 'Theorem 2.2 (Revised)' which states that the proposed reduction does not guarantee an equivalence and that the NP-hardness claim remains open. Immediately after, it asserts that the theorem has several implications (NP-hardness, inapproximability, FPT-intractability) and says 'We prove Theorem 2.2 in Appendix A'. This is self-contradictory: the revised statement admits the proof is invalid, yet the paper still claims the consequences as if the theorem were proven. The implications are therefore unsubstantiated, and the claim of a proof in the appendix contradicts the retraction in the main text.

After presenting Theorem 2.3 (a PTAS for complete graphs with a fixed number of intervals, allowing any overlap pattern), the text states: 'Due to these challenges, while a PTAS is feasible for limited and well-structured interval overlaps, the general case requires further algorithmic innovations beyond current methods.' This claim directly contradicts Theorem 2.3, which already provides a PTAS for all possible overlap structures (by enumerating all 2^{O(k^2)} patterns). The statement misrepresents the scope of the result and undermines the theorem's validity.
